verified.exploit_entry_point: Real loopback HTTP requests against an in-process Tomcat: a Servlet 3.0 web application (WEB-INF/web.xml plus programmatic registration from a ServletContainerInitializer) and a context launched through the embedded Tomcat API. The suites deploy, start and drive the container through its normal request path; no product helper is used to compute an expected value.
sites: java/org/apache/catalina/core/StandardContext.java:4365-4374 (no marker for a servlet created through createServlet)
java/org/apache/catalina/core/StandardWrapper.java:1078 (no ServletSecurity scan when the servlet is loaded)
java/org/apache/catalina/authenticator/AuthenticatorBase.java:484 (no scan before constraints are looked up)
java/org/apache/catalina/startup/ContextConfig.java:367-372 (no authenticator when no constraint is visible at CONFIGURE_START)
java/org/apache/catalina/core/ApplicationServletRegistration.java:166-187 (addMapping does not re-apply a stored security element)
java/org/apache/catalina/core/StandardContext.java:5599-5650 (constraints computed from the mappings known at call time)
java/org/apache/catalina/deploy/SecurityConstraint.java:517-556 (dynamically created collections are marked as descriptor collections)
routes: T1: action rules declared on a servlet registered through createServlet (web application and embedded context), on a descriptor-declared servlet, with a role, with a method constraint; PERMIT and descriptor-priority are the coupled positives
T2: any constraint added by a ServletContainerInitializer (programmatic registration), and the same in an embedded context, where no authenticator exists at all
T3: setServletSecurity followed by addMapping (one or several patterns) and the inverse order; role rules added after mapping
T6: a servlet mapped at a path ending in the form-login action name, reached with a real authenticated session

All 12 pass on the pinned tree and the reference through the full verifier; the hidden security/functional suites were also matrix-run against every check patch, and the first-fix recall patch was run through the full verifier with all functional tests passing.

traps.shape: ServletSecurity annotations on programmatically registered servlets are never read at the pinned commit: createServlet-created instances are not marked for scanning, no scan runs before the constraint check, and a descriptor-declared servlet's annotation is ignored. The fix must scan at first use, keep descriptor rules winning, and handle role and method shapes.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Annotation-declared security is developer convenience; the deployment descriptor (or the registration API the application calls) is the authoritative place to declare constraints, so an application that really cares lists them in web.xml.
traps.realistic_because: published fix site for GHSA-mg4v-rf8p-ghqq (CVE-2011-1088): the annotation consumer is simply absent from the pinned tree, exactly as the advisory describes

traps.shape: No authenticator valve is installed when no constraint is visible at CONFIGURE_START, and the embedded launcher installs none at all. Every programmatic constraint arrives from a ServletContainerInitializer after that phase, so the rule is added but nothing enforces it.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Only an application that adds constraints through the Servlet 3.0 registration API is affected, and such an application can also install its own authenticator valve, so the container is not expected to reconfigure itself.
traps.realistic_because: published fix site: the first upstream fix removed the empty-constraint early return and added an authenticator to the embedded launcher

traps.shape: setServletSecurity computes constraints only from the mappings known at that moment (the pinned code carries a TODO saying so). A mapping added afterwards is unprotected; the natural deferral to the end of start-up would push the constraint past the authenticator decision, so the fix must couple mapping registration with constraint refresh.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: addMapping is specified as an initialisation-time operation and normal applications map first and then set the rules, so a snapshot of the mappings looks complete.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the pinned method documents that constraints cannot be computed until all mappings are known

traps.shape: The form-login action is exempted from role checks by a suffix match on the request path, so a servlet mapped at a path ending in that name skips its declared roles. The fix must narrow the exemption while keeping the real action reachable.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The form action is the login endpoint and must stay outside the constraints, and no servlet is normally mapped under a URI ending in that name, so the suffix test looks like harmless login plumbing.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the suffix exemption predates the advisory and survives every published fix commit

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the guard is evaluated against the request path that reaches the servlet; no proxy or neighbouring object exists on this surface
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: each tested rule names one role and every request method and direction share the same guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: no read/write or verb split exists; every method reaches the same constraint check
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the mapper decodes the path before the guard and the guard uses that same value; no adjusting step sits between them
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: identity is a servlet role name compared literally; no parser sits on this path
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the authority is the container's own realm; a missing principal is an ordinary unauthenticated request that the suite requires to be refused

A.summary: ServletSecurity annotations are not followed; access restrictions can be bypassed

B.summary: Security constraints are not followed when the deployment has no login configuration; incorrect fix for CVE-2011-1088
